title: Houthi Missile and Drone Attacks on Saudi Arabia Send Brent Crude Surging to $108 Intraday, Settling Up 3.4% at $106.60
detail: Yemen's Houthis claimed missile and drone strikes on Saudi Aramco facilities at the Red Sea export hub of Yanbu and a 'sensitive target' in Riyadh on Sep 24. The Saudi-led coalition said its air defenses intercepted six ballistic missiles aimed at Taif and Yanbu, while a Greek Patriot battery stationed near Yanbu shot down an additional missile and drone. Oil markets reacted immediately: Brent crude, which had slid to $98.44 on Sep 23 after Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline restart, spiked as high as $108.23 intraday before settling up 3.4% at $106.60/bbl -- reversing two days of de-escalation gains -- with WTI following a similar path. The move underscored that Gulf export infrastructure remains vulnerable even as US-Iran diplomacy continued on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York.

title: 80-Nation Coalition at UN Demands Urgent Reopening of Strait of Hormuz, Condemns Iranian Restrictions and Houthi Attacks
detail: Bahrain's Foreign Minister Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani read a joint statement on behalf of roughly 80 countries at the UN General Assembly in New York on Sep 24, demanding 'full restoration of navigational rights and principles without delay,' urgent reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, and safe transit for vessels 'without the imposition of tolls, conditions, or illegal charges.' The statement condemned Iran's restrictions on the strait in place since the Feb 28 outbreak of the US-Israeli war and renewed Houthi attacks on Red Sea shipping and Saudi Arabia, citing a strike that killed an Indian crew member aboard a commercial vessel off Oman. 'Commercial shipping and seafarers must never be used as leverage,' Al Zayani said, adding 'the threat we face remains very real and continues to grow.' Diplomats said the coalition was weighing follow-up measures at the UN Security Council to enforce naval protection corridors.

media.caption: Bahrain's FM Al Zayani reads an 80-nation joint statement demanding the Strait of Hormuz reopen
